transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-03
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jonah Kim (Redwood SE); Sara Li (ClearPath, Head of ML); Carlos Mendes (ClearPath, CTO); Priya Rao (ClearPath, PM)

Summary (auto-gen - may be rough):
Quick run-through of competitive messaging and a demo script. Goal to align on talking points for the pilot and to rehearse answers on security and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Topics: messaging, competitive positioning, demo flow, security/compliance Qs, pilot logistics

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the account, Jonah is our SE who will run the demo today.
[00:07] Sara: Hi, Sara here - appreciate it. We wanted to use this session to rehearse the messaging we give to our execs and also see a tight demo.
[00:12] Carlos: Yeah, thanks. Busy week so we'll be brief, want to see the performance story.
[00:16] Jonah: Cool, thanks. We'll do a short 10-minute messaging recap, then a 20-minute demo, then Q&A and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:23] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:26] Maya: Quick housekeeping - this is internal enablement / rehearsal so we might role-play some customer Qs. Also FYI our security pack link is in the meeting notes.
[00:33] Sara: Got it.

[02:00] Jonah: Ok starting with messaging. Top-line: Redwood is a developer-first inference platform focused on predictable performance and cost controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Emphasize production guarantees - autoscaling, observability, rollouts.
[02:15] Carlos: When you say predictable performance, like what SLA or metrics do you typically quote?
[02:20] Jonah: We talk in p95 latency targets per model and per-capacity class, and throughput guarantees for Dedicated. For sales convos we frame it as "latency SLOs + predictable throughput" - that resonates with platform teams.
[02:30] Maya: Also call out caching and batching efficiency - we save token cost with prefix / KV caching which matters for high-volume flows.
[02:38] Sara: KV cache - is that like a per-session cache? Sounds similar to what we built in-house.
[02:43] Jonah: Right, it's a combination of prefix caching and KV cache for multi-turn. Helps especially for assistant style workloads. Note - sometimes the transcription shows K-V cash or VPC as VPCe, so we'll just say KV cache in docs.

[05:10] Priya: Competitive angle - customer asks about OpenAI or Anthropic. What should we say?
[05:16] Maya: For operators we highlight: 1) unified runtime across deployment modes (hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) so they don't re-architect, 2) cost control levers - batching, quant profiles, intelligent routing, and 3) production-grade observability.
[05:31] Jonah: Tactically, when they mention OpenAI: emphasize our routing and dedicated pools for compliance/regulatory customers, and our ability to run in VPC or on-prem with managed control plane. For Anthropic or Cohere - emphasize our verifiable performance profiles and tooling to map model variants to cost/latency needs.
[05:49] Carlos: Customers will push on price vs latency though.
[05:52] Maya: Yes - admit tradeoffs: for ultra-low latency at all costs, some single-tenant providers might be slightly cheaper in latency but lack our unified tooling and rollout controls. Then pivot: show how efficient batching and prefix caching reduces token spend which offsets infra cost.

[08:00] Jonah: Demo prep - I'll run a live assist flow: ingestion -> contextual retrieval -> generation with tool calls, show streaming and token-level cost breakdown in the console. We'll also flip over to Dedicated config and show scaling settings.
[08:13] Sara: Can we see an example of private deployment network topologies? We're evaluating VPC peering and an on-prem option.
[08:19] Jonah: Yes. We'll show VPC options, KMS integrations, and audit log screenshots. Note: some words in the auto-transcript might say K-M-S as KMS or K M S - but we just mention Key Management Service and HSM when needed.

[10:30] Maya: Role-play: Carlos you're an internal skeptic - ask about SOC2 and data residency. Jonah will answer as the SE.
[10:36] Carlos: Ok, uh - SOC2 is table stakes for us. Do you have proof, and how does Redwood handle logs and encryption?
[10:42] Jonah: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts. For logs we support tenant-scoped audit logs and you can route audit exports to your SIEM. For encryption, default at-rest plus optional customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). We can get you the attestation docs.
[10:58] Carlos: How about data residency in EU?
[11:02] Jonah: We support region pinning and private deployments in specific regions; on-prem for full residency.

[13:00] Sara: Another common question - how do you handle model rollouts and regressions? We need to show we can catch quality regressions.
[13:06] Jonah: Good call - mention per-model rollouts, canary and A/B testing, automatic fallback policies, and Redwood Optimize monitors prompt-based eval sets and emits regression alerts.

[15:20] Jonah: Ok jumping into demo - sharing screen.
[15:24] [screen share noise] Jonah: Here is the Console, top-right you can see the token-level breakdown per request, per route. I'm running a sample conversation - notice streaming and ability to do function/tool calls, and how the KV cache reduces repeated context tokens.
[15:40] Priya: Nice. That cost breakdown - can we export that to CSV for ingestion into our FinOps tools?
[15:46] Jonah: Yes, export and APIs available.

[18:00] [demo continues; Jonah narrates steps and shows Dedicated config] Jonah: This is the Dedicated config page - you can pin model versions, choose GPU types, and set autoscale policies. Also we have burst capacity options for spikes.
[18:18] Sara: For benchmarks, what's the typical delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[18:22] Jonah: Hosted is our managed pool - low friction. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable latency; typical p95 improvement depends on load but customers often see more stable p95 and higher throughput per commit. We can quantify in the pilot.

[21:10] Carlos: One tangent - can Redwood run our eval harness? We have 5000 prompts and want side-by-side with OpenAI models.
[21:17] Jonah: Yes - we'll coordinate the benchmark. We prefer a controlled pilot window where we run your prompts against configured model variants and measure latency, tokens, and cost.
[21:26] Maya: That's a key next step - Jonah can scope the test plan.

[24:00] Priya: Objections practice - I'm playing procurement. How do you justify unit economics to finance if per-token costs look higher?
[24:09] Maya: Tie it to total cost of ownership - include savings from fewer re-runs thanks to better quality, lower dev ops overhead because of our unified runtime, and caching/batching wins which reduce token counts. Also present Hosted to Dedicated migration path so they see potential discounts on committed capacity.

[26:30] Jonah: Quick note on quantization - we have quant profiles that can reduce GPU memory and cost; good to mention for customers asking about latency/cost tradeoffs.

[28:40] [role-play wrap] Carlos: Ok, that felt good. A couple of tough Qs - what about lock-in?
[28:46] Maya: Answer: we avoid lock-in by enabling standard model formats, offering export paths and by supporting BYO model where customers bring their own weights in Private. But also acknowledge migration effort and show how our runtime reduces long-term ops burden.

[31:10] Jonah: Back to demo, I'm going to show the routing policy UI - you can route by region, cost, or latency, and set fallbacks. This helps with graceful degradation during capacity issues.
[31:25] Priya: If a region fails, does traffic automatically failover to another region?
[31:29] Jonah: Yes if you configure it - we recommend a canary first. Also can set degradations to slower model variant rather than full failover.

[33:50] Maya: Ok let's outline final ask for pilot - we'll run a 2-hour controlled benchmark: your 5k prompts, a hosted vs dedicated vs private run (if you want), measure p50/p95, tokens per response, and cost. Jonah will design the test and share the plan.
[34:05] Carlos: That sounds reasonable. Timeline?
[34:08] Jonah: We can do the pilot week of 2026-10-12 if you confirm scope early next week.
[34:14] Priya: I'll confirm by 10/07.

[36:00] Maya: Great. Any other product Qs?
[36:04] Sara: One last ask - can you provide a short one-pager for executives that compares Redwood vs OpenAI/Ecosystem?
[36:10] Maya: Yes, we'll prepare a competitive one-pager emphasizing deployment modes, observability, and cost levers.

[38:30] Jonah: A quick demo note - occasionally the automated transcript will swap model names or say "Readwood" instead of Redwood; ignore that in the shared notes.

[40:00] Maya: Wrap up - recap of next steps: Maya sends pricing + security docs; Jonah preps pilot and test prompts; Priya confirms pilot scope and attendees.
[40:12] Carlos: Thanks all.
[40:15] Sara: Thanks, very helpful.
[40:17] Priya: Thanks everyone.

[44:30] [call ends]

Notes: transcription contains typical ASR errors (speaker mis-attrs, minor word swaps). Shared artifacts: link to security pack (docs/redwood-security.pdf), pricing template (sheets/redwood-pricing-example), demo recording (video/demo-2026-10-03.mp4).
